changes.change: The sales tax rate on invoice lines changes from its current value to 9%.
location_reasons: Tax multiplier is hardcoded as 1.08 (8% tax). Must change to 1.09 to reflect the new 9% sales tax rate used in SubmitInvoice total calculation.

MAX_LINES comment says 'Max 10 lines per invoice' but value is 25 — unrelated, but MAX_AMOUNT threshold (line 9) and ERR_AMOUNT_LIMIT check (line 22) must be re-tested because the higher tax rate will increase totals, potentially causing previously-passing invoices to now exceed MAX_AMOUNT=100000.

RecalculateTotal uses a different tax multiplier of 1.07 (7%). This is already inconsistent with SubmitInvoice (1.08). With the change to 9%, this method must also be evaluated and updated to 1.09 if it is intended to reflect the same tax rate, or the discrepancy must be explicitly justified.

usp_SaveInvoice contains a business rule that overrides APPROVED status to PENDING_APPROVAL when @Total > 50000. With a higher tax rate (9% vs 8%), invoice totals will be larger, meaning more invoices will cross the 50000 threshold and be demoted to PENDING_APPROVAL. This logic must be re-tested against the new tax-inclusive totals.

The CHECK (Total > 0) constraint and DECIMAL(12,2) column definition must be re-verified to ensure the new tax-inclusive totals still fit within the column precision and satisfy the constraint under edge cases.
predicted_rules: Invoice line totals are calculated as Qty * UnitPrice * 1.08 (8% sales tax); this multiplier must change to 1.09 (9% sales tax) in SubmitInvoice.
The maximum invoice total allowed is 100,000; with a higher tax rate, previously-valid invoices near the limit may now exceed ERR_AMOUNT_LIMIT and be rejected.

Invoices with total > 50,000 submitted with APPROVED status are automatically demoted to PENDING_APPROVAL by the stored procedure; more invoices will now cross this threshold due to the higher tax rate.

Vendor codes starting with 'ZZ' receive automatic APPROVED status; this auto-approval combined with the new tax rate increases the likelihood of the >50,000 demotion rule being triggered for ZZ vendors.
RecalculateTotal uses a 7% tax multiplier (1.07), which is already inconsistent with SubmitInvoice (1.08); both must be reconciled to 9% (1.09) if they are intended to represent the same tax rate.
The IsOverdue 30-day rule is not affected by the tax rate change.
The LegacyDiscount 2% discount is not affected by the tax rate change, but if applied post-tax its monetary effect will change due to higher tax-inclusive totals.
predicted_reports: Any invoice total or tax summary report consuming the Total column from the Invoice table (totals will be higher for all new invoices)
Any approval-rate or PENDING_APPROVAL vs APPROVED status distribution report (more invoices will be demoted by the >50,000 rule in usp_SaveInvoice)
Any report using RecalculateTotal output (currently uses 7% tax, inconsistent with the 8% stored value and the proposed 9%)
predicted_contracts: SubmitInvoice public API (InvoiceService.vb lines 11-30): return value behaviour changes — more callers will receive ERR_AMOUNT_LIMIT for high-value invoices; ZZ-vendor callers may receive PENDING_APPROVAL instead of APPROVED for invoices between ~45,872 and 50,000 pre-tax

usp_SaveInvoice stored procedure (schema.sql lines 15-24): the @Total > 50000 threshold check will be triggered more frequently due to higher tax-inclusive totals, changing the stored Status for a broader set of invoices

RecalculateTotal public API (InvoiceService.vb lines 32-38): currently returns a different tax rate (7%) than SubmitInvoice (8%); any external caller relying on this value for reconciliation will see a changed result if updated to 9%

Field device external API documented as 'Max 10 lines per invoice' (comment line 7) but enforcing MAX_LINES=25: no change to line limit, but callers near the amount limit will experience new rejections due to higher per-line tax

changes.change: Increase the automatic approval ceiling for ZZ vendors from 50000 to 75000.
location_reasons: The stored procedure usp_SaveInvoice contains the hard-coded ceiling of 50000 that overrides APPROVED status to PENDING_APPROVAL for ZZ vendors. This threshold must be raised to 75000 to implement the change.

MAX_AMOUNT is set to 100000. Although it does not encode the 50000 ceiling directly, it must be re-tested to confirm the new 75000 ceiling does not interact unexpectedly with the overall amount limit, and any documentation/comments referencing approval thresholds here should be reviewed.

The SubmitInvoice method sets status to APPROVED for ZZ-prefixed vendors unconditionally in application code, then relies on the stored procedure to demote to PENDING_APPROVAL above the ceiling. The interaction between this logic and the new 75000 ceiling in the stored procedure must be re-tested to ensure the end-to-end approval flow is correct for totals between 50000 and 75000.

Total calculation and MAX_AMOUNT guard must be re-tested against the new 75000 ceiling to verify no edge-case overlap between the approval ceiling and the amount limit, particularly for ZZ vendors submitting invoices near 75000.
predicted_rules: ZZ-prefixed vendors whose invoice total exceeds 50000 are automatically demoted from APPROVED to PENDING_APPROVAL; this ceiling must be raised to 75000.
ZZ-prefixed vendors are granted automatic APPROVED status in the application layer; the boundary at which that approval is preserved now extends from totals up to 50000 to totals up to 75000.
Invoices with totals between 50000 (exclusive) and 75000 (inclusive) submitted by ZZ vendors will now be stored with status APPROVED instead of PENDING_APPROVAL.

The overall invoice amount limit of 100000 remains unchanged, but the approval tier boundary within that limit shifts, creating a new effective range (75000–100000) where ZZ vendor invoices are still demoted to PENDING_APPROVAL.
predicted_reports: Any report filtering or aggregating invoices by Status (APPROVED vs PENDING_APPROVAL) for ZZ vendors, as the population of auto-approved invoices will grow to include totals up to 75000
Any audit or compliance report tracking invoices that bypassed manual approval, as more high-value ZZ-vendor invoices will now appear in that set
Any financial exposure or liability report based on automatically approved invoice totals, as the maximum auto-approved value per invoice increases from 50000 to 75000
predicted_contracts: usp_SaveInvoice (SQL stored procedure) — its internal business rule threshold changes from 50000 to 75000; any caller relying on the demotion behaviour for values between 50000 and 75000 will observe different output status

SubmitInvoice public API (InvoiceService.vb) — the observable return value for ZZ-vendor invoices with totals between 50000 and 75000 changes from PENDING_APPROVAL to APPROVED; field devices or downstream consumers of this return value must be re-tested

Invoice table (schema.sql) — the distribution of Status values written to the Invoice table changes, affecting any downstream ETL, integration, or system reading invoice status directly from the database
